hints: Factorise $3\tan^2 x - 5\tan x - 2 = 0$ as $(3\tan x + 1)(\tan x - 2) = 0$.
Solve $\tan x = 2$ and $\tan x = -\frac{1}{3}$ for $x$ in $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Factorise the quadratic equation in $\tan x$:
$$3\tan^2 x - 5\tan x - 2 = 0 \implies (3\tan x + 1)(\tan x - 2) = 0$$

Set each linear factor equal to zero:
$$\tan x = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad \tan x = -\frac{1}{3}$$

Find all solutions in the interval $0^\circ \le x \le 180^\circ$:
$$\text{From } \tan x = 2: \quad x = \tan^{-1}(2) \approx 63.4^\circ$$
$$\text{From } \tan x = -\frac{1}{3}: \quad x = 180^\circ - \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = 180^\circ - 18.43^\circ \approx 161.6^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } x = 63.4^\circ, \quad 161.6^\circ)$$

hints: For $3\tan^2 x - 5\tan x + k = 0$ to have no real solutions, set the discriminant $\Delta < 0$.
walkthrough:
For the quadratic equation in $\tan x$ to yield no real roots, its discriminant must be strictly negative:
$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac < 0 \implies (-5)^2 - 4(3)(k) < 0$$
$$25 - 12k < 0 \implies 12k > 25 \implies k > \frac{25}{12}$$

hints: Identify that $\tan x = 0$ is the only value giving two solutions in $[0^\circ, 180^\circ]$ ($0^\circ$ and $180^\circ$).
Substitute $\tan x = 0$ into the equation to find $k = 0$.
Solve $\tan x(3\tan x - 5) = 0$ for all three solutions.
walkthrough:
A single value of $\tan x$ provides only one angle in $[0^\circ, 180^\circ)$, except for $\tan x = 0$, which provides two solutions ($x = 0^\circ$ and $x = 180^\circ$).
Thus, $\tan x = 0$ must be a root of the quadratic equation:
$$3(0)^2 - 5(0) + k = 0 \implies k = 0$$

Substitute $k = 0$ into the quadratic equation and factorise:
$$3\tan^2 x - 5\tan x = 0 \implies \tan x(3\tan x - 5) = 0$$
$$\tan x = 0 \implies x = 0^\circ, \quad 180^\circ$$
$$\tan x = \frac{5}{3} \implies x = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \approx 59.0^\circ$$

State the constant $k$ and all three solutions:
$$k = 0; \quad x = 0^\circ, \quad 59.0^\circ, \quad 180^\circ$$
